subject: Clarify Novum output rights, training consent & feedback license
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@novumcorp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum Procurement <procurement@novumcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on output & training clauses in redline v3

Hi Michael / Laura,

Thanks for sending the MSA redline (v3). Legal ran through the sections related to customer content and model training and had a couple of substantive questions before we escalate to our CISO and procurement committee:

1) Section 7.2 (Output ownership): your redline currently says "Customer retains ownership of outputs." Can you confirm whether that includes downstream productization (i.e., embedding outputs into our product UX or training internal models on outputs)? Our counsel wants explicit carveouts if Redwood intends to use customer outputs for model improvements.

2) Section 9.1 (Feedback & telemetry): Novum is comfortable providing feature feedback but wants assurance that any feedback used for model tuning will be anonymized and not surfaced to other customers. Is a scoped, non-attributional feedback license something Redwood can accept?

3) Data retention and logs: procurement asked whether audit logs containing customer prompts would be retained beyond 30 days and if so, how they are segmented between hosted vs. dedicated deployments.

We attached our internal summary (redline_summary.pdf). Can we get a short call this week to avoid multiple rounds with our procurement/legal team?

Best,
Elena Suarez
Head of Legal Operations
NovumCorp

---
Attachment: redline_summary.pdf (PDF, 82KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@novumcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on output & training clauses in redline v3

Elena —

Thanks for the clear summary and the helpful PDF. Quick answers up front, then a proposal for next steps:

- Output ownership: You (Novum) retain title to the outputs generated from your inputs. We are happy to add explicit language that customer-owned outputs can be productized by you (embed in UI, distribute downstream) without Redwood claiming ownership.

- Training/Model improvements: Our standard hosted offering asks for a limited feedback license to improve models, but we can respect a strict opt-out or scoped license for enterprise customers. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can commit to "no customer output ingestion for model training" unless explicitly agreed in writing.

- Feedback anonymization: We can accept language requiring non-attributional use of feedback and a section that prohibits exposure of identifiable customer outputs to third parties.

- Logs/retention: Hosted: default 90 days for prompt logs; Dedicated: configurable per contract (we can set 30 days). We should document this in a table in the order form.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Laura (legal) to propose precise redline language (we'll prepare suggested text for Sections 7.2 and 9.1).
2) Priyom will share a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a call slot.
3) If Novum prefers a stricter training exclusion for hosted, we can offer a priced add-on to lock-in a training-opt-out.

Can you do Thu 4/22 10:00am PT?

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@novumcorp.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on output & training clauses in redline v3

Hi Elena —

Thanks for surfacing these. A few clarifications from Redwood legal to reduce churn:

- Output/Productization (Section 7.2) — Suggested clause: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in outputs and may use, reproduce, and incorporate such outputs into Customer products, provided Customer will not present Redwood's underlying models or training data as Customer's own proprietary training corpus." This keeps it clear that outputs are theirs while protecting model provenance.

- Training/Feedback (Section 9.1) — We propose two mutually exclusive options you can pick in the order form:
  a) Standard: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, irrevocable license to use de-identified feedback for model improvements (default for hosted).
  b) Enterprise Opt-Out: Customer may elect an enterprise opt-out (applies to Hosted only) where Redwood will not ingest customer outputs or feedback for model training; pricing and SLA adjustments apply.

- Telemetry & Logs — We'll add a table to the order form that states retention defaults and per-deployment customizations. For hosted, we will add a clause guaranteeing anonymization controls and a meeting with our CISO for high-sensitivity customers.

I'll prepare redline text and upload to the shared DocuSign draft. If Novum prefers some compromises (e.g., allow de-identified examples for benchmarking with express permission), we can include an explicit approval flow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Procurement flagged two pragmatic constraints that will drive negotiation speed:
- Novum's procurement wants a hard 30-day retention cap for hosted prompts unless CISO signs off.
- They prefer an opt-out by default for training ingestion (to avoid lengthy legal approval), and will accept a priced opt-in if they need Redwood to use outputs for model tuning.

I'll draft a short mutual action plan with Milestones: redline language by 4/23, Novum legal review by 4/25, sign by 5/3 contingent on pricing confirmation. Also capturing a single call slot Thu 4/22 10:00am PT (tentative).

Elena —

Thanks again for the quick review. Per our internal sync, attached are: (1) a clean suggested clause for Output/Productization; (2) two options for Feedback/Training (standard vs enterprise opt-out); (3) a short redline summary table mapping hosted vs dedicated defaults (retention, logging, training ingestion). See Novum_MSA_redlines_v3.docx.

Summary of decisions we propose for the MAP:
- Novum selects Enterprise Opt-Out for training ingestion on Hosted by default; Redwood will offer a priced add-on to enable training ingestion later.
- Hosted prompt logs retention set to 30 days for Novum; we will document this in the order form and in the security addendum.
- Output ownership language updated to explicitly permit Novum to productize outputs.

Can you confirm acceptance of the three bullets above in reply? If yes, we will convert the updated doc to the DocuSign draft (link included) and circulate the pricing addendum for the training opt-in option.

Call options remain Thu 4/29 10am PT or Fri 4/30 8am PT if you prefer live walk-through.
